basis: Exactly one actual original approved PNG load per figure. Frozen before reading any modern author observation or comparing modern figure candidate.

figures.pixelAppearance: Black-and-white natural waterside illustration, with irregular shore, vegetation, rough rock surfaces and many uneven water-ripple strokes. Not a calibrated geometry chart.

objects.observation: An irregular connected shore/bank occupies the left side and curves into the lower foreground; it is not an isolated geometric obstacle or a third detached water rock.
Upright branching vegetation with uneven foliage occupies the left bank, including a narrow upper-left stem/crown and fuller lower-left foliage. No species or exact tree count is printed.
A large, craggy exposed rock projects above the water in the middle-right region. Its silhouette, interior white breaks and dark rough strokes are natural-object identity, not a measured polygon.
A separate much smaller exposed rock is near the right edge, lower than the upper ripple bands. It is distinct from the large rock and from the connected left shore.

objects.countMeaning: One repeated water-wave/ripple family, not a printed numerical wavefront count.
objects.observation: Many broadly transverse, roughly parallel but uneven dark ripple strokes fill upper/right water and the foreground. They pass close to the small rock. Strokes terminate or bend near the shore and large rock.

A comparatively unlined water patch lies below/left of the large exposed rock, bordered by visible ripple strokes. The white region has no printed zero-amplitude mark, shadow boundary line or quantitative measurement.

waveRelationships.pixelFact: Two detached rock obstacles have clearly different apparent sizes.
waveRelationships.rawContextFact: The source text compares the small obstacle with the wavelength and the larger obstacle with a wavelength-sized scale; no numerical size or wavelength is given.

waveRelationships.pixelFact: Ripple strokes occupy the water close around the small rock; no extensive unlined region like the large-rock region is drawn there.
waveRelationships.rawContextFact: The source uses the small stone to illustrate waves bending around an obstacle.

waveRelationships.pixelFact: The large-rock region and adjacent less-lined water contrast with the surrounding rippled water.
waveRelationships.rawContextFact: The source-era passage describes the larger obstacle's shadow categorically. Do not turn the illustration's white paper into a modern quantitative assertion of exactly zero field.

fidelityRequirements: Preserve natural rock and bank/vegetation identities, the two detached obstacles and their size contrast.
Preserve the qualitative small-rock access versus large-rock less-lined-region contrast, without inventing a calibrated boundary or exact propagation arrow.
Repeated ripple strokes are a wave-family observation, not permission to invent a source numerical count or strip the visible family down to one line.

figures.pixelAppearance: Monochrome oblique-perspective water-tray apparatus illustration. The visible water-wave marks are line strokes, not a photographic water texture or a calibrated plot.

objects.observation: One low quadrilateral tray is seen obliquely, with a rear rim, side rims, a long front wall and short dark support/foot details below the front.
A single bounded water surface lies inside the tray rims and contains both incident and transmitted wave families.
A thick near-horizontal rod enters from the left, crosses the left rim and reaches the left-hand water region.
A prominent oblique drive/paddle-like stroke is at the rod's inner end in the left wave region. Its mechanical drive is not separately shown or labelled.
A roughly front-to-back oblique screen divides incident left water from transmitted right water. Two aligned screen portions leave one small interruption/opening near the middle.
The gap between the screen portions is visibly narrow compared with the wider gap in figure98; no gap dimension or ruler is drawn.
Several successive, approximately parallel/slanted incident crests occupy the left water region, aligned with the source-side apparatus and screen perspective.

Successive curved fronts fan into the right water region from the small screen opening. Near-opening short curved fragments and larger outer arcs all belong to this transmitted family; some outer strokes meet the tray limits.

waveRelationships.pixelFact: There is one screen aperture between two screen segments, and the strongly curved wavefront family occupies the other side of that aperture.
The right-hand fronts fan out with approximately nested curvature around the aperture region.
waveRelationships.rawContextFact: The source describes a slit smaller than the wavelength and circular water waves, approximately like emission from a point source.

waveRelationships.pixelFact: No plotted origin, centre point, radius, wavelength tick or precise spacing value is printed.
waveRelationships.constraint: A future deterministic wave layer must express the source's aperture/curvature relationship, not claim the perspective strokes are exact measured circles or fabricate source numerical ratios.

fidelityRequirements: One tray, one entering rod and its visible paddle-like stroke, one two-part screen with one narrow aperture.
Preserve incident near-parallel versus transmitted curved/fanning fronts and the aperture-centred qualitative relationship.
Do not replace visible repeated fronts with an arbitrary decorative sine squiggle, add a solved measurement, or invent a source arrow.

figures.pixelAppearance: Monochrome oblique-perspective water-tray apparatus illustration matching the comparison setup of figure97; the water-wave marks are line strokes, not a visible photographic water texture.

objects.observation: One low oblique quadrilateral tray, with outlined rear/side rims, long front wall and dark foot/support details below the front.
One bounded water surface contains incident left and transmitted right wave regions.
One thick near-horizontal rod enters from the left across the rim and reaches the source-side wave region.
One conspicuous oblique paddle-like drive stroke is near the rod's inner end; no separate motor or temporal control is depicted.
Two aligned front/rear oblique screen portions leave one broad open central section. The opening is appreciably wider than in figure97.
One large aperture between the screen ends opens the left wave region to the right; no dimension, scale or printed ratio is provided.
Successive approximately parallel oblique wave strokes appear on the left side, as in the narrow-aperture comparison.

Successive right-side fronts remain mainly straight/parallel and occupy the region aligned with the opening; they do not become the fully fanning arc family of figure97. Front ends show limited edge curvature.

waveRelationships.pixelFact: The opening is broader than figure97, while the same basic rod/tray/screen comparison apparatus remains present.
waveRelationships.rawContextFact: The source describes a slit larger than the wavelength.

waveRelationships.pixelFact: The transmitted family is largely straight/parallel, in contrast to the narrow-aperture fan.
There is limited curvature at the ends/edges of the transmitted fronts, not an explicit zero-wave shadow boundary.
